corpus.statement: EIGHT DOCUMENTS IS THE CORPUS, and it stays eight until production traffic adds to it. This is an enumeration, not an estimate: on 2026-09-30 all six sandbox MinIO buckets were listed in full (4061 objects), every PDF under every sustainment prefix was fetched and hashed, and the result was 8 distinct document contents -- every one of which is already a TARGETS row, and every TARGETS row of which has a PDF. There is no unseen notice sitting in the bucket. The corpus therefore does not widen by looking harder; it widens when new notices are ingested. Enumerated in docs/pcn-corpus-widening-2026-09-30.md, which also lists the extensions present and absent corpus-wide.
corpus.why_it_is_here: This block exists so the denominator lives where the GATE READS IT rather than only in prose. pcn_corpus_run.check_ground_truth() asserts TARGETS against it at startup and aborts on a disagreement, and pcn_corpus_gate.py copies it into docs/corpus-gate/latest.json so a committed report states the corpus it was measured against. A denominator that only a human can check is a denominator that drifts.
corpus.nine_vs_eight: Both numbers are correct and neither is a defect to fix. The harness scores 9 FILENAMES; two of them -- Diodes_PCN_2683_FULLGREEN.pdf and Diodes_PCN_2683_Rev1_EOL.pdf -- are ONE document content (md5 abe083fe...) ingested under two names, so that document is scored twice at 402 parts. Hence 898 harness parts over 496 distinct ones: 402 of the 898 is the same notice counted a second time. Keep the 9 rows -- the duplicate pair is how the two-ingest case is exercised -- and never quote 898 as a count of distinct parts.
corpus.widens_when: A new notice is ingested into processing-artifacts/sustainment/inbound/**. Then: add its TARGETS row, add its part numbers to notices{} under the same verbatim-presence rule as every other entry, and raise scored_entries / distinct_documents / gt_parts / distinct_parts here. Re-enumerating the bucket does NOT widen it -- that was done, and found nothing new.
